topics.topic: A31 concurrency review coverage of INV-009 after its move to A3
questions: Must the concurrency review now reference A3 and name the single-active assignment and grant guarantee, or is INV-009 intentionally excluded from this security category despite A31 claiming a total review?

After INV-009 moved from A8 to A3 and gained storage-enforced uniqueness for three access-record kinds, must the concurrency category reference A3 and name concurrent assignment/grant creation as affected, or is INV-009 intentionally outside this security-review category?

Now that INV-009 and its storage-enforced single-active-record guarantee moved from A8 to A3, must the concurrency category reference A3 and explicitly cover concurrent creation of staff assignments, viewer grants and producer grants?

quotes:
The total review of `SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` over States 0–2 as migrated.
It decides nothing new: each applicable category is owned by a decision above.

- Every category has an explicit outcome: APPLICABLE resolves to an accepted decision, UNRESOLVED to an open question, and NOT_APPLICABLE carries its project-specific rationale (`SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md`).

INV-009 moved here from A8 on 2026-11-22: it is the lifecycle of `GrantStatus`
records, not an idempotency identity, and A8's owner `snapshot_import` held a
rule the access modules carry out (State 3 round 57). It now covers staff
assignments too and allows a new record after revocation (owner 2026-11-22,
`open_questions.md` Q29 (a); State 1 M04, M07, M15).
- concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A8, A18, A19, A22, A29; affected: replay identities, single active budget version, bootstrap
judgement.divergence: A reviewer who follows the moved invariant treats concurrent creation of all three access-record kinds as covered by A3, while a reviewer who follows A31's recorded references inspects A8 and omits INV-009; the security reviewer or auditor observes the difference, and the omission violates A31's explicit-outcome guarantee.
judgement.why: After INV-009 moved from A8 to A3, A31 leaves its concurrency outcome unstated because the applicable category neither resolves it to A3 nor excludes it with a project-specific rationale.
options: Add A3 and single-active staff assignments, viewer grants and producer grants to the concurrency category.
Declare explicitly that INV-009 is not part of the concurrency review and give the project-specific rationale.
Leave the existing A8 reference as if it still owned INV-009.
consequences: Adding A3 makes the moved storage-enforced access-record guarantee part of the applicable concurrency review.
An explicit exclusion supplies the project-specific rationale required for a non-applicable outcome.
Leaving A31 unchanged lets reviewers silently omit a concurrency guarantee while A31 still claims a total review.

topics.topic: Required behavior and history preservation after multiple revoke-and-regrant cycles
questions: What must the Required tests show when a pair has two or more revoked historical records and no active record: must another new active record be created while every revoked record remains unchanged?
What must the Required tests show when a pair has multiple revoked historical records after repeated revoke-and-regrant cycles and no active record?

Must the required test show that every operation can create another active record when the pair already has multiple revoked historical records, preserving all of them, rather than only when its sole record is revoked?

quotes: - INV-009: at most one active record per (staff_id, project_id) assignment, per (viewer_id, project_id) grant and per (service_principal_id, project_id) grant; revoked records of the pair stay, and a new grant after revocation is a new record

- INV-009: at `assign_staff_project`, `grant_viewer_project` and `grant_producer_project`: a pair whose only record is revoked receives a new active record and the revoked one is unchanged; a pair with an active record is refused and nothing changes; and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check.

A revoked assignment is
  terminal and no operation reactivates it; assigning the pair again creates
  a new assignment record.

A revoked grant is
  terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again
  creates a new grant record.

A revoked grant is terminal and no
  operation reactivates it; granting the pair again creates a new grant
  record.
judgement.divergence: After two completed revoke-and-recreate cycles, an implementation may either create another active record while preserving both revoked records or fail because it assumes only one predecessor; the administrator observes the runtime result, while the current Required tests can miss the failing behavior because they require only a pair whose sole record is revoked.
judgement.why: State 2 requires unbounded retained history and renewed access after revocation, but its Required tests specify only the single-revoked-record case and therefore do not say that the invariant must be shown after multiple cycles.
options: Require repeated revoke-and-create cycles for staff assignments, viewer grants and producer grants, proving that any number of revoked records may coexist with one new active record.
Test only the single-revoked-record case, leaving behavior with multiple revoked records unverified.
consequences: Repeated-cycle coverage demonstrates that all revoked history remains and another active record can be created.
Single-predecessor coverage can pass even if an implementation refuses or fails once more than one revoked historical record exists.
judgement.requirement: - INV-009: at most one active record per (staff_id, project_id) assignment, per (viewer_id, project_id) grant and per (service_principal_id, project_id) grant; revoked records of the pair stay, and a new grant after revocation is a new record

witness.initial: A staff/project pair has two revoked StaffProjectAssignment records and no active assignment after two completed assignment-and-revocation cycles.
events: An administrator calls `assign_staff_project` for the same pair again.
outcomes: A new active assignment is created and both revoked assignments remain unchanged.
The operation refuses or fails because it assumes that at most one revoked predecessor exists, while the stated single-revoked-record test still passes.
witness.observer: The administrator and the Factory verification gate.
basis:
A revoked assignment is
  terminal and no operation reactivates it; assigning the pair again creates
  a new assignment record.

topics.topic: Duplicate-active failure contract and translation of concurrent uniqueness collisions
questions: What failure may callers rely on when an active duplicate is detected, and must a storage uniqueness collision caused by a concurrent request be translated to the same failure?
What failure may callers rely on when an active assignment or grant already exists?

When concurrent requests both pass the active-record check and the storage rejects one, must the losing operation return the same duplicate-active refusal as an ordinary duplicate, or may it return a storage/internal failure?

quotes:
inactive project; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active assignment;
`RegistryBoundaryError`.
or non-active viewer; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant.

inactive project; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant;

SqliteStaffAccessRepository.insert_staff_assignment: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST assert open state through the context and append every StaffProjectAssignment field with parameterized SQL and canonical serialization; a duplicate assignment_id, and a second assignment for a (staff_id, project_id) pair that already has one, MUST both surface as a translated persistence error rather than a silent overwrite.

SqliteViewerAccessRepository.insert_viewer_grant: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST assert open state through the context and append every ProjectViewerGrant field with parameterized SQL and canonical serialization; a duplicate grant_id, and a second grant for a (viewer_id, project_id) pair that already has one, MUST both surface as a translated persistence error rather than a silent overwrite.

SqliteServiceIdentityRepository.insert_producer_grant: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST assert open state through the context and append every ProducerProjectGrant field with parameterized SQL and canonical serialization; a duplicate grant_id, and a second grant for a (service_principal_id, project_id) pair that already has one, MUST both surface as a translated persistence error rather than a silent overwrite.
| `AuthorizationRejected` | `authorization_guard` | 403 |
| `PersistenceError` | `portal_store` | 500 |
judgement.why: State 5 assigns AuthorizationRejected to an active duplicate found by the operation but requires a uniqueness collision at each SQLite insertion boundary to surface as translated PersistenceError, so sequential and concurrent duplicate attempts intentionally have distinct observable failures.
options: Expose one duplicate-active conflict for both the operation check and a storage collision.
Expose AuthorizationRejected for the operation check but PersistenceError for a storage uniqueness collision.
Expose only an undifferentiated refusal in both cases.
consequences: The later contract chooses distinct failures: an ordinary duplicate is HTTP 403 and a raced storage collision is HTTP 500, while both preserve the single-active invariant and write nothing for the loser.

topics.topic: State-preservation assertions after storage-level insertion refusal
questions: Must the storage-level Required test also assert that the rejected insertion leaves the existing active record, all revoked history, and all other state unchanged?

topics.topic: Whether storage-level uniqueness tests must cover all three access-record kinds
questions: Must the Required tests demonstrate storage-level rejection independently for staff assignments, viewer grants, and producer grants, or is one representative storage check sufficient?

quotes: - INV-009: at `assign_staff_project`, `grant_viewer_project` and `grant_producer_project`: a pair whose only record is revoked receives a new active record and the revoked one is unchanged; a pair with an active record is refused and nothing changes; and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check.
- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal].
- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:viewer_access_sqlite_uow_client_portal].
- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].
judgement.why: The Required tests name all three creation operations and bind INV-009 to separate service-identity, viewer-access and staff-identity checks, so the storage-level guarantee is required for every access-record kind rather than one representative kind.
options: Demonstrate the storage guarantee for all three record kinds
Demonstrate only the viewer and producer grant stores
consequences: All three storage implementations must reject a second active record for their respective pair identity.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
